newsitem.title: UK: Merck renews attack on UK drug pricing.
newsitem.headline: Merck renews attack on UK drug pricing.

text.p: Merck, Sharpe & Dohme (MSD), the British subsidiary of U.S. drugs giant Merck & Co, said on Tuesday that the UK's system for controlling drug prices is stifling the industry's development.

In a renewed attack on the system, known as the Pharmaceutical Price Regulation Scheme (PPRS), MSD managing director Vincent Lawton said Britain was "in danger of losing its position as the leading location for pharmaceutical companies to invest."

In a speech to a deregulation and inward investment seminar organised by the Social Market Foundation, Lawton said: "The PPRS is more than an administrative burden. It represents an unparalleled intrusion by government into how private companies conduct their affairs."

The PPRS was established in 1978 as a voluntary agreement, renegotiatied every five years, between the government and the drugs industry. The scheme limits the total profit that a company can make from selling to Britain's National Health Service.
The government sets a profit target for individual companies expressed as a percentage return on capital employed (ROC).

Lawton said the PPRS is a "bricks and mortar scheme," which rewards investment in constructing buildings but actually discourages intellectual investment and "restricts how much capital we are allowed to employ for exports."

"This is old-fashioned regulation promoting old-fashioned results," said Lawton. "Our future lies in our capacity to pioneer new drugs, new technologies, to extend the boundaries of medicine and science."
Lawton called for deregulation of drug pricing, pointing to the success of deregulation in Britain's telecommunications industry, which had "encouraged the development of a world-beating industry."
The MSD managing director is chairing a task force on the PPRS for the Association of the British Pharmaceutical Industry (ABPI).
The next review of the PPRS is due in 1998.
